what_this_is: Eight controlled failures planted in what the Core returns or in the result set's own bookkeeping. Five are numerical; three are structural and leave every residual looking healthy, which is why the integrity checks exist.

control.note: The control is NOT expected to be clean. MV-A fails its preregistered tolerance at every held-out point and MV-C fails at six of 371, both for reasons adjudicated in the findings, and the split check reports the one-row discrepancy recorded as MVA-1. What the control establishes is the BASELINE each plant is measured against, so a plant only counts if it makes things worse.

plants.plant: +5 percent systematic bias on every Core open-circuit voltage
plants.how_it_is_caught: a 165 mV bias on a 3.3 V cell leaves the millivolt-scale tolerance

plants.plant: resistance-temperature slope 2 percent too steep, exact at the reference point
plants.how_it_is_caught: the deviation stops being the omitted quadratic term, so the ratio metric leaves its band

plants.plant: every Core open-circuit voltage multiplied by 1000
plants.how_it_is_caught: a kilovolt where a volt was measured

plants.plant: the relaxed open-circuit voltage read at 1 h instead of 24 h
plants.how_it_is_caught: the cell has not finished relaxing at 1 h, so every declared endpoint and every held-out value moves

plants.plant: a calibration point duplicated into the held-out set
plants.how_it_is_caught: the leakage check finds one set of inputs carrying two splits

plants.plant: measurement uncertainty set to zero on a passing case
plants.how_it_is_caught: a comparison scored against a zero uncertainty is refused outright

plants.plant: a row screened OUT_OF_SCOPE relabelled as validation
plants.how_it_is_caught: the applicability check refuses an out-of-scope row carrying a validation verdict

plants.plant: one failing held-out point relabelled as calibration
plants.how_it_is_caught: the split check counts the rows that actually ran against the counts the plan fixed
